17a2b8b182: This service puts your prints in a heat-binding cover and melts the glue with heat to make them into a book. The order is: choose a cover and pay → warm up → put it in the machine → timer → cool for 10+ minutes. Great for theses · reports · contracts.

It uses glue. No hole punching, no springs or strings.
Put the pages in so their edges touch the glue inside the cover, and the binder's heat melts the glue to stick them.
f4908af05c:
Each cover has a set number of sheets it can hold. You can put in only up to the number written on the cover. (Depending on the store, it's written as '매' or '장'. Both mean "sheets".)
There are 20 · 40 · 60 · 80 · 100 · 120 · 150 · 180 · 200-sheet covers.
2c0dff762d: The price is 1,500 won per cover, no matter how thick.
0e66d5646b:
Too few sheets can't be bound.
e.g.) 5 or 10 sheets won't work even with a 2mm cover. The empty space at the glued edge is too big, so it won't stick.
7387b8a082:
No cover that exactly fits your number of sheets?
Take 2 covers close in thickness to your number of sheets, try your pages in each, and use the one that leaves less empty space.
e.g.) For 110 sheets, try both the 10mm and 12mm covers.

4b63d357a4:

Never open it right after taking it out.
Put it in the cooling tray or on a flat surface and let it cool for 10+ minutes before opening.
The thicker it is, the longer than 10 minutes — wait until the side is no longer hot and the glue inside the cover has fully cooled and hardened.
7129c5a14c:
📌 In the cooling tray, stand it with the closed end (glue side) down.
Don't put it in upside down.
9c85e20504: 🚨 Always let it cool! If you open it before the glue hardens, all the pages will fall out.
